title: Nourishing Dense Japanese Baby New Potatoes Onigiri
description: A cultured and dense one-pot Japanese dish featuring baby new potatoes, nigiri-shaping, and Buddhist-temple-friendly ingredients, served in a ramekin.
instructions: Rinse the Japanese rice thoroughly and soak it in water for 30 minutes.
Drain the water and cook the rice according to the package instructions.
In a large pot, combine the halved baby new potatoes, 2 cups of water, and 1 teaspoon of salt, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
In a small pan, heat the sesame oil over medium heat and cook the chopped scallions until fragrant.
Add the cooked scallions, dried seaweed, and pickled plum to the cooked rice and mix well.
Divide the rice mixture into 6 equal portions and shape each portion into a triangle using a ramekin as a mold.
Fill the center of each triangle with a few pieces of the cooked baby new potatoes.
Serve the onigiri warm or at room temperature.
Garnish with additional chopped scallions and dried seaweed if desired.
